newsitem.title: HONG KONG: NBC expands channels into two million Indian homes.
newsitem.headline: NBC expands channels into two million Indian homes.

text.p: National Broadcasting Co said on Thursday its NBC and CNBC channels were now available in two million Indian homes under an expanded distribution deal with Indian cable television provider IN CableNet.

"Both of our channels are available today in those two million homes," Stuart Goldfarb, NBC's senior vice-president and managing director of worldwide business development, said by telephone in Hong Kong.

"We see India as one of the most vibrant and dynamic cable markets in Asia -- 15 million cable subscribers, a strong middle class, a good amount of consumer spending and a great hunger for quality international programming."

The U.S.-based broadcaster, a unit of General Electric Co, has been offering its 24-hour entertainment and information channel NBC and its business news counterpart CNBC in India since October through IN CableNet.
But limitations in the country's television infrastructure meant only about 600,000 subscribers were seeing anything.

"You have severe channel capacity problems on cable systems in India and you also have severe channel capacity problems in Indian homes -- many Indian TVs at home do not get above Channel 14," Goldfarb said.
The new arrangement moves NBC and CNBC into the prime band of the first 14 channels, providing full access to IN CableNet's subscriber base, he said.
"With this deal, we far surpassed where we expected to be this year," Goldfarb said.
IN CableNet, part of India's Hinduja group, provides cable throughout India but has most of its subscribers in Bombay and Delhi, he said.
The arrangement was not exclusive, he said, adding that NBC was "in constant conversations with other cable operators".
NBC is on the AsiaSat 2 satellite, with STAR TV acting as the distribution agent to Indian cable operators, Goldfarb said.

Delhi-based Television Eighteen Entertainment Ltd will supply local programming for the NBC channel and General Electric subsidiary IGE India recently completed a studio in Bombay to produce local programming for CNBC, he said.

Besides dealing a blow to competitor Asian Business News (ABN), the addition of the new Indian subscribers meant CNBC now reaches six million homes in the Asia-Pacific region and NBC reaches four million, he said.
Goldfarb said NBC is distributed in Hong Kong, Taiwan, China, Australia, Thailand, South Korea and Japan, among other places.
